Completed Matrix from a Bayesian PCA Imputation

Source: R/mi_pca_s3.R
as.matrix.si_mi.Rd

Fill the missing values of obj with one draw from a finalized fit.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'si_mi'
x[...]

# S3 method for class 'si_mi'
as.matrix(x, draw = 1L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'si_mi_pca'
as.matrix(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A si_mi object. A finalized fit, from mipca(), mipca_fit() or mipca_finalize().

...

Not used.

draw

Integer. The kept draw that fills the missing values, from 1 to the number of kept draws. Defaults to 1.

Value

A numeric matrix.

Details

The completed matrix. A completed matrix is obj with its missing values filled by one draw, on the scale of obj. The observed values are unchanged, and the row and column names are kept. A fit made with subset gives a matrix of the selected columns only.

Which draws. print() shows the number of kept draws. They are numbered chain by chain: with k draws per chain, draws 1 to k are the first chain's, k + 1 to 2 * k the second's, and so on.

Multiple imputation. Call as.matrix() once per draw. Draws evenly spaced from the first to the last are spread across the chains. Each completed matrix is a full copy of obj, so m of them take m times its memory. On a large obj, use each matrix in turn instead of keeping all of them.

Refusals. A resumable fit, made with keep_state = TRUE, is refused. Finalize it with mipca_finalize() first. [ does not work on a finalized fit: choose the columns with subset when fitting, or subset a completed matrix.

See also

  • mipca() to make a finalized fit.

  • mipca_finalize() to finalize a resumable fit.

Examples

set.seed(1)
sim <- sim_mat(n = 50, p = 20, beta = TRUE)
fit <- mipca(sim$input, rank = 2, transform = "logit_biwhiten", seed = 1)
fit
#> si_mi fit: 50 x 20, 100 imputed cells, 400 draws
#>   next: as.matrix() with 'draw' for a completed matrix, summary() for Rhat and ESS

# The matrix completed by draw 10
x10 <- as.matrix(fit, draw = 10)

# Five completed matrices, at draws spread over the 400 kept
b <- round(seq(1, 400, length.out = 5))
completed <- lapply(b, function(d) as.matrix(fit, draw = d))
